correspondsTo: BLOCKER-5 (getDefinition) and BLOCKER-6 (NEW_COUPLED_BLOCKER_DISCOVERED - the same getDefinition behavior bypassing the otherwise-correct ambiguous-DEFINITION-amendment protection)
priorEvidence: tests/contract-model/part-b-recert-blocker2-6-tools-adversarial.test.ts (originally committed to PROVE the defect; now updated to prove it is fixed)
oneRootCauseTwoConsequences: The Part B recertification treated these as one root cause with two named consequences, and this fix follows the same framing: getDefinition (lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic/tools.ts) silently served raw, stale, pre-amendment definition text labeled only 'source: base-document' - textually indistinguishable from a term that was never amended at all - whenever a real, on-file OperativeProvisionView for that exact term existed but its currentText was honestly null (an AMBIGUOUS/PARTIAL amendment target resolution, operative-state.ts's own rule). FINDING-2 is that defect in getDefinition itself (BLOCKER-5's own named failure-mode class recurring on a branch the prior Workstream B per-tool audit did not fully trace - it checked only the happy path where operative.currentText was truthy). FINDING-3 is the direct, unavoidable consequence: this is also an unguarded bypass around BLOCKER-6's own otherwise-correct ambiguous-DEFINITION-amendment protection (cross-reference-audit.ts's candidateSourceNodeIds-based coverage-audit mechanism) - that mechanism itself was independently re-verified correct and untouched by this fix; getDefinition simply routed around it through a different module (the LLM tool-calling surface, not the coverage-audit surface).

endToEndTrace_termResolutionToEvidencePa.1_termResolution: getDefinition.execute({term}) first calls findProvisionView(access.operativeState?.provisions, term) - the SAME lookup helper getOperativeProvision, getRelatedAmendments, and getPriorVersion all already use, matching either sectionRef or definedTermRef. This step was already correct and is unchanged.
endToEndTrace_termResolutionToEvidencePa.2_sourceNodeLookup: When no OperativeProvisionView exists for this term at all (no recorded amendment activity, ever), the ORIGINAL code fell through directly to getScopedDefinitionFullText -> StructuralIndex.getDefinitionFullText, which resolves via a plain .find() over the document's own definitions array - silently the FIRST match on a collision. This step is where the SECOND gap (see below) lived.
endToEndTrace_termResolutionToEvidencePa.3_amendmentEffects: buildProvisionView (amendment/operative-state.ts) already correctly derives targetResolutionStatus/status/currentText from the real amendment chain BEFORE getDefinition ever sees it - this computation was never the defect. The defect was entirely on the CONSUMING side.
endToEndTrace_termResolutionToEvidencePa.4_operativeState: operative-state.ts's own OperativeProvisionView.currentText is set to null whenever targetResolutionStatus !== 'UNIQUE' (AMBIGUOUS or NOT_FOUND target) OR the provision is genuinely CONFLICTED OR its structural health is unsafe - this is the single, already-correct, already-audited source of truth for 'can this term's current text be confidently stated.'
endToEndTrace_termResolutionToEvidencePa.5_returnedEvidencePayload_THE_DEFECT: getDefinition's execute() body gated its ENTIRE amended-text branch on `operative?.currentText` being truthy (`if (operative?.currentText) { ...return 'amended'... }`). Any other case - operative existing but currentText null (AMBIGUOUS/PARTIAL/CONFLICTED/structurally-unsafe) - fell through to the SAME raw-base-document branch a genuinely never-amended term would also reach, with the SAME 'source: base-document' label and ZERO disclosure of `operative.status`, `targetResolutionStatus`, or `unresolvedIssues`. This is the exact defect the Part B recertification reproduced.

fix.mechanism: getDefinition.execute() now checks only whether an OperativeProvisionView exists for this term at all (`if (operative) { ... }`), not whether its currentText happens to be truthy. Inside that branch, status/unresolvedIssues are ALWAYS disclosed, and the returned text is `operative.currentText ?? "(no current text recorded)"` - the IDENTICAL placeholder string getOperativeProvision's own raw-fallback branch already uses for the same null case. This is a verbatim structural mirror of getOperativeProvision's own 'found' branch (`if (view) { return ok({ sectionRef, status: view.status, currentText: text, ... }) }`), not a new, independently-invented disclosure format.
fix.secondGapFoundAndFixed: A second, related gap was found while tracing step 2 above and is required by this phase's own invariant ('Multiple candidate definition occurrences -> never guess; disclose ambiguity'): the no-recorded-amendment fallback (a term with NO OperativeProvisionView at all, because it was never touched by any amendment) used to call getScopedDefinitionFullText, which silently returns the FIRST of 2+ colliding physical definitions of the same term in one document via StructuralIndex's own .find(). This is a real, live, never-amended drafting-collision case operative-state.ts had already solved for the AMENDMENT-TARGET-RESOLUTION side (resolveUniqueDefinitionByRef, used internally by resolveBaseText) but which getDefinition's own base-document fallback never consulted. Fixed by exporting resolveUniqueDefinitionByRef from amendment/operative-state.ts (it was module-private) and reusing it, unchanged, in getDefinition's fallback loop (home document first, then real instrument siblings, mirroring getScopedDefinitionFullText's own existing ordering) - an AMBIGUOUS result is refused with an honest reason and candidate count, exactly mirroring getOperativeProvision's own resolveUniqueNodeByRef-based refusal for a colliding SECTION reference.
fix.whyReuseGetOperativeProvisionsDiscipline: The task's own architecture requirement is explicit: use the SAME temporal/operative discipline getOperativeProvision already correctly implements, never invent a second, parallel mechanism. Concretely this fix (a) reuses the identical OperativeProvisionView/OperativeStateStatus/findProvisionView primitives already in tools.ts, (b) reuses the identical '(no current text recorded)' placeholder string, (c) reuses the identical resolveUnique*ByRef ambiguity-refusal pattern (resolveUniqueNodeByRef for SECTION in getOperativeProvision; resolveUniqueDefinitionByRef for DEFINITION in getDefinition, both now living in and exported from amendment/operative-state.ts), and (d) introduces zero new status vocabulary, zero new OperativeContractState field, and zero new disclosure format. The only genuinely new code is the export of one already-existing private function and the two call sites that now use it.

invariantMapping.CURRENT_or_uniquely_resolved: operative view has currentText truthy (status OPERATIVE_STATE_RESOLVED in practice, though the fix discloses whatever the real status is) -> returned confidently as before, WITH status now also disclosed (never a behavior change for this case beyond the added field).
invariantMapping.KNOWN_SUPERSEDED: Not a distinct OperativeProvisionView.status value for DEFINITION-kind provisions in this codebase (supersession status is a NODE-level concept - see getNodeSupersessionStatus - not a provision-level one); the analogous provision-level states this fix actually gates on are CONFLICTED/PARTIAL/REVIEW_REQUIRED, all handled uniformly below.
invariantMapping.AMBIGUOUS_or_PARTIAL_amendment: operative view exists, currentText is null -> status/unresolvedIssues disclosed, placeholder text returned, stale figure never served as confident current fact. (This fix does not additionally re-serve the stale text labeled 'historical' - it follows getOperativeProvision's own established choice of a placeholder over a raw-text re-serve for this exact null case, per the phase's own 'do not invent a second mechanism' instruction.)
invariantMapping.no_operative_state_available: access.operativeState is null entirely, OR no view exists for this term -> unchanged from before for the 'null entirely' case (already handled by the outer `access.operativeState ?` guard); for 'no view for this term specifically,' now resolved via the ambiguity-safe fallback below rather than the old ambiguity-blind one.
invariantMapping.multiple_candidate_definitions: no operativeState view (never amended) AND 2+ colliding physical definitions in the resolved document -> refused outright with an honest candidate count, never guessed. NEW behavior (previously silently guessed the first match).

otherDefinitionAccessPathsAudited.methodology: grep -rn 'getDefinitionFullText|\.getDefinition\(' across lib/contract-model, then read every call site to determine whether it (a) has access to operative-state/amendment information, (b) discards or never consults a real, on-file ambiguity signal, and (c) serves the result to an LLM caller or the compiler as though it were settled fact.
otherDefinitionAccessPathsAudited.amendment/pipeline.ts_getTargetCurrentTe: Genuinely the SAME gap. The SECTION branch already correctly refused to guess on a colliding legal reference (resolveUniqueNodeByRef). The DEFINITION branch called index.getDefinitionFullText(term, documentId) directly - silently the first match on a same-document definition collision - and fed the result straight into interpretAmendmentClause's own real LLM call as the amendment target's authoritative 'targetCurrentText,' with no disclosure that it might be the wrong one of 2+ colliding definitions. Fixed with the exact same primitive (resolveUniqueDefinitionByRef) rather than a third parallel check; AMBIGUOUS now returns null, mirroring the SECTION branch's own established contract. See lib/contract-model/compiler/amendment/pipeline.ts's own updated comment for detail. This is a directly-required, in-scope fix (same root-cause class, same audit instruction, same reused primitive) - not a re-litigation of an already-certified boundary.
otherDefinitionAccessPathsAudited.coverage-audit/definition-audit.ts_and_c: Both call StructuralIndex.getDefinitionFullText directly with no operativeState parameter at all. Neither is an LLM-facing evidence tool nor a compiler input - both are deterministic, structural, sub-structure-signal comparisons (does the bundle's stored excerpt contain the same inclusion/exclusion/cap/etc. keywords the real full text does) that produce persisted AuditFinding rows for human/coverage review, never a claim that the retrieved text IS the current, settled definition. Out of scope for this invariant; no gap of the relevant class found.
otherDefinitionAccessPathsAudited.context-retrieval/pipeline.ts_and_defini: Phase 2D's own retrieval (which builds the CovenantContextBundle DEFINITION/DEFINITION_DEPENDENCY items later served through getContextBundleComponent/getSharedCapContext) has zero operative-state awareness by design - confirmed by grep, and already disclosed in tools.ts's own header comment on the BLOCKER-5 fix for those two tools. This is not a case of a real signal being discarded (there is no operative-state input here to discard); it is already handled at the CONSUMPTION boundary via summarizeItemWithSupersession's fail-closed UNKNOWN_SUPERSESSION_STATUS for any item with no structuralNodeId (which every DEFINITION-type item is). That boundary was BLOCKER-5's own already-certified fix and is unchanged here. Per this phase's scope discipline, context-retrieval/** is excluded from this workstream absent a direct requirement, and none was found.
otherDefinitionAccessPathsAudited.amendment/independent-verification.ts_NO: Already independently re-derives a genuine three-way UNIQUE/AMBIGUOUS/NOT_FOUND resolution for DEFINITION targets via its own document-scoped uniqueness check (deliberately NOT sharing operative-state.ts's own resolveUniqueDefinitionByRef, per Architecture Invariant #17's 'the system that proposes and the system that checks must not be the same pass') - this module never serves definition TEXT to an LLM at all; it only gates RESOLVED vs REVIEW_REQUIRED. No gap found; already fixed in an earlier phase (Phase 3F.1.4 Workstream D §6C) and correctly kept independent, so it was not touched.
otherDefinitionAccessPathsAudited.amendment/operative-state.ts_itself_NOT_: This module IS the authoritative source of the honest UNIQUE/AMBIGUOUS/NOT_FOUND and RESOLVED/PARTIAL/REVIEW_REQUIRED/CONFLICTED signal every other module in this audit either correctly consults (getOperativeProvision, independent-verification.ts) or, prior to this fix, incorrectly discarded (getDefinition, pipeline.ts's getTargetCurrentText) - it is the producer, not a consumer with a gap of its own.

scopeDisciplineNote: amendment/pipeline.ts is not on the excluded list (lib/contract-model/analysis/orchestrator.ts, lib/contract-model/compiler/context-retrieval/**) and was touched only because the task explicitly instructs auditing 'any OTHER definition-access path in the codebase' with 'the same gap' after fixing the main tool - this is precisely that: the same root-cause class, fixed with the same already-exported primitive, in one function, with zero touches to BLOCKER-2/3/4's own certified orchestrator/context-retrieval machinery.

requiredEndToEndTest.construction: A real StructuralIndex holding a stale, pre-amendment definition of a material covenant-basket term ($8,000,000), paired with a real OperativeContractState whose one DEFINITION-kind OperativeProvisionView for that exact term is AMBIGUOUS/OPERATIVE_STATE_PARTIAL (2 colliding physical occurrences, real amendment effect, target could not be uniquely attached) - directly modeled on the same fixture shape the Part B recertification's own BLOCKER-6 'Chain 2' construction and the adversarial test use. Compiled through the REAL RealSemanticCaller.compile() tool-use loop and the REAL compileCovenantToIR()/normalizeSubmission() - only the Anthropic client itself is scripted (mirrors caller-tool-discipline.test.ts's own established convention). This exercises the real ToolRunner, the real getDefinition.execute(), and the real deterministic post-processing end to end - never a mock of any of that production logic.
requiredEndToEndTest.test1_honoredDisclosure: The scripted model calls getDefinition, then submits a definition with sufficiency AMBIGUOUS, citing the disclosed uncertainty. Assertions: (a) the ACTUAL tool_result bytes the model received mid-loop (client.sentMessages, not a direct isolated tools.ts call) never contain the stale $8,000,000 figure and DO contain OPERATIVE_STATE_PARTIAL/AMBIGUOUS - proving the fix is live-wired through the real compilation loop, not merely correct in isolation; (b) the honest AMBIGUOUS sufficiency survives unchanged through real normalizeSubmission()/IR validation to the final compiled IRDefinition.
requiredEndToEndTest.test2_architecturalProofOfRealStakes: A CONTRAST test with the identical fixture: a model that IGNORES the disclosure and dishonestly submits sufficiency COMPLETE for the same term. Result: the dishonest COMPLETE is NOT deterministically downgraded by anything downstream (confirmed both through the real pipeline result and directly against normalize.ts's own enforceSufficiencyConsistency, called with operativeLineage: null - the same null normalize.ts's own definitions branch always passes, unconditionally, at line ~397). This is the concrete proof that the fix is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: normalize.ts's ONE deterministic sufficiency backstop is never wired to a DEFINITION's own operative status at all (lineage is only ever computed at the candidate/rule level, per the candidate's own anchored structuralNodeIds - independently confirmed by the Part B recertification's own task4.blocker6 finding, 'operativeLineage in normalize.ts is computed from the CANDIDATE's own anchored provision/structuralNodeIds - never from every defined term a tool call happened to resolve during compilation'). Before this fix, getDefinition's own disclosure was the ONLY thing that could ever inform an honest model's sufficiency judgment for a term like this; with the tool silently serving a confident-looking stale figure, there was no way for even a well-intentioned model to know to be honest. After this fix, the information exists; test 1 confirms an honest model can and does act on it, and test 2 confirms (as an architectural fact, not a defect introduced by this fix) that nothing else in the pipeline currently would have caught a model that did not.
requiredEndToEndTest.downstreamMachineryConfirmedUnableToReac: Per test 2's own finding, the ONLY mechanism standing between an on-file DEFINITION amendment ambiguity and a falsely-confident COMPLETE reaching persisted IR is the evidence the compiling model is actually shown. This fix makes that evidence honest. It does NOT (and was not asked to) add a second, definition-level deterministic backstop to normalize.ts - that would be a different, larger architectural change outside FINDING-2/3's own scope (the required fix is 'bring getDefinition to getOperativeProvision's own disclosure standard,' not 'invent per-definition operativeLineage'), and BLOCKER-6's own already-certified cross-reference-audit.ts mechanism remains the real downstream backstop for the RULE-level consequence of an ambiguous definition (a rule whose economics depend on the term), operating independently on MaterialSemanticUnit anchors rather than on which tools a compiler call happened to invoke.

finalDisposition: FINDING-2 (BLOCKER-5, getDefinition): CLOSED. getDefinition now discloses the real operative status (and unresolvedIssues) in every branch where an OperativeProvisionView exists for the queried term, exactly mirroring getOperativeProvision's own already-correct discipline, and refuses rather than guesses when the base document itself has 2+ colliding un-amended definitions of the same term.
